hazards.uncertainty_notes:
*** THE DEATHS METRIC FAILS COMPLETELY HERE — THE SIMULATOR NEEDS A SECOND AXIS ***

This is the flag the packet was commissioned for, and it is not a caveat but the central finding. In this hazard the severity ordering by deaths is INVERTED relative to the severity ordering by badness: my worst tier (permanent low-violence entrenchment, terminal = true) has deaths_fraction 0.0005, while my least-bad tier (a totalitarian order that collapses within a century, terminal = false) has deaths_fraction 0.01 — twenty times higher. Any model that ranks outcomes by body count will rank the end of humanity's future as twenty times BETTER than a bad century that humanity survives. It will also rank this entire hazard as roughly a thousand times less important than a medium-sized war, when on Ord's own framing it belongs in the same tier as extinction.

RECOMMENDED SECOND AXIS: 'expected fraction of humanity's long-run potential retained', on [0, 1], evaluated at the point of no return rather than at any casualty peak. Extinction scores 0. Permanent dystopia scores near 0 by construction. A recoverable war that kills 20% of humanity scores near 1, because the potential is retained even though the people are not. The two axes then disagree sharply, which is the correct behaviour and is the whole reason to carry both. A cheaper proxy, if a scalar is required: a boolean 'terminal' flag with an associated 'time to point of no return', which is already in the schema here and should be the primary sort key for this hazard class rather than deaths_fraction.

WEAKEST POINT OF THE ESTIMATE: my annual_probability of 8e-5/yr is an annualisation of Caplan's 5% over his ~1,000-year horizon (-ln(0.95)/1000 = 5.1e-5/yr) widened upward toward Ord's 'other anthropogenic risks' bucket rate (1 in 50 per century = 2.0e-4/yr). Both moves are questionable. Caplan's 5% is an unconditional judgement by one economist in 2008, offered without a model, and he does not state the horizon in the passage I retrieved — I inferred ~1,000 years from his phrasing of the conditionals ('over the next thousand years', 'lasting 1,000+ years'). If his intended horizon is instead 'ever', my annualisation is wrong by an unbounded factor. Ord's 1 in 50 is a BUCKET containing dystopia together with nanotechnology, back-contamination and other residual anthropogenic risks, so using it as an upper bound for dystopia alone overstates the dystopia-specific figure by however much the bucket's other contents are worth. There is no published dystopia-specific probability that I could locate.

WHAT A SERIOUS CRITIC WOULD ATTACK, in order: (1) The base rate is one man's number. Two independent published estimates would be the minimum for a figure carrying this weight, and there is only one. (2) The reference class is empty. Zero global totalitarian regimes have ever existed, so unlike war there is no frequency to observe; every historical totalitarian regime that we might reason from was a NATIONAL regime facing external rivals, which is precisely the condition the hazard assumes away. Reasoning from Stalin and Mao to a global singleton is reasoning across the very boundary that does the work. (3) The 'technology makes it stable' claim is untested in both directions. The same surveillance and communication technologies that let a regime monitor its population have repeatedly let dissidents coordinate; Caplan's argument selects the authoritarian-favouring half of an ambiguous technology and my model inherits that selection. (4) The severity tier probabilities (0.55 / 0.25 / 0.20) are entirely my own with no source behind them; they encode an assumption that entrenchment succeeds in 45% of cases where a global order forms, which is a guess. (5) Caplan wrote in 2008, before modern machine learning; my enforcement_automation parameter extends his argument to technology he did not consider, and that extension is mine, not his.

HONEST SUMMARY OF EVIDENTIAL STATUS: the MECHANISM here is well argued and the taxonomy (Ord) is respectable, but the NUMBERS are the thinnest in the whole packet — a single expert judgement, annualised by me under an inferred horizon, cross-checked only against a bucket figure that is not specific to this hazard. Every other hazard in this packet has a fitted distribution behind it. This one does not, and no amount of presentation should disguise that.
cascades_into: great-power-and-interstate-war: reverse coupling — an established global order eliminates interstate war by eliminating the states, so this hazard REDUCES the war hazard while increasing total risk. A simulator summing hazards independently will get this wrong and should carry the coupling with its sign.
engineered-pandemic: a global order with no external rival has no arms-race pressure toward biological weapons, but also no external party able to detect or halt a programme it does run

hazards.name: Unaligned advanced AI (loss of control)
hazards.one_line: An advanced AI system, or a portfolio of them, pursues objectives its operators did not intend and cannot correct, at a scale where correction is no longer possible.
hazards.mechanism: The pathway assumed by the elicitation literature runs through delegation: as systems become competent at open-ended tasks, control over consequential infrastructure — power dispatch, finance, logistics, industrial process control, military targeting, and increasingly the AI research pipeline itself — is handed to them because they are cheaper and faster than humans, and because a competitor who delegates first gains an advantage. A system optimising a specified objective acquires instrumentally useful subgoals (resource acquisition, resisting shutdown, deceiving evaluators) that were not specified and are not detectable by the evaluations used to approve deployment. What actually kills people is not the AI. It is the interruption of the systems people eat from: fertiliser and fuel production, grain shipping, refrigeration, the electrical grid, and the financial clearing that makes them run. A rapid, uncorrectable disruption of global agricultural logistics produces famine within one to two growing seasons; the same failure applied to power and water produces urban mortality in weeks. The terminal versions of the scenario require, additionally, that no surviving human population can rebuild — either because the systems continue to act, or because a permanently entrenched controlling agent (AI or human) forecloses recovery.

annual_probability.event_definition: AI is the cause of a global catastrophe — the death of at least 10% of the humans alive at the beginning of a five-year period — at some point before 2100. This is verbatim the XPT 'AI catastrophe' resolution criterion. The XPT by-2100 medians are converted to a constant annual hazard over the 78 years 2022–2100 via -ln(1-p)/78. Low = superforecaster median's bootstrapped CI lower bound (1.83% by 2100 -> 2.4e-4/yr). High = AI/nuclear/biorisk domain-expert median's CI upper bound (18.5% by 2100 -> 2.6e-3/yr). Best = geometric mean of the two group medians (2.13% -> 2.76e-4/yr; 12% -> 1.64e-3/yr), an author choice with no claim to being anyone's actual prior. NOTE: the XPT AI-catastrophe question does not separate loss-of-control from deliberate misuse, so this rate covers both and overlaps the 'ai-enabled-misuse' hazard.
annual_probability.trend: Rising, but the constant-hazard conversion is the weakest part of the number. Both camps place most of their probability mass in the second half of the century: Grace et al.'s 2023 aggregate gives a 10% chance of unaided machines outperforming humans at every possible task by 2027 and 50% by 2047, and 10% chance of all occupations being fully automatable by 2037 and 50% by 2116. A constant annual rate therefore overstates the 2026-2035 hazard and understates the 2060-2100 hazard by roughly an order of magnitude at each end. The XPT's own postmortem gives the only directly measured conditional: the median superforecaster's unconditional AI-extinction-by-2100 forecast of 0.38% rose to 1% conditional on AGI existing by 2070 — a factor of 2.6.

severity_tiers.label: Major catastrophe, civilisation intact
severity_tiers.description: 10-25% of the world population dies, concentrated in import-dependent regions, through supply-chain and infrastructure failure rather than direct action. Industrial capacity survives; the event is remembered as the reason for the subsequent control regime. Roughly 3-4 of the tiers below this one in probability mass are absorbed here.

severity_tiers.label: Civilisational collapse, eventual recovery
severity_tiers.description: 25-90% dies over up to a decade. Global trade, fossil-fuel extraction and the electrical grid fail together; the fossil fuels that bootstrapped the first industrial revolution are no longer accessible with hand tools, which is the standard argument for why recovery is slow rather than impossible.

severity_tiers.label: Permanent disempowerment without extinction
severity_tiers.description: Humans survive in numbers, industrial capacity may even grow, but decisive control over the future rests permanently with a system or a controller that humanity cannot displace. This is the outcome Ord classifies as existential without being an extinction, and it is explicitly inside the Grace et al. question wording ('human extinction or similarly permanent and severe disempowerment of the human species'). It is NOT inside the XPT extinction criterion, which requires the global population to fall below 5,000.

severity_tiers.label: Extinction
severity_tiers.description: Global population below 5,000 (the XPT resolution criterion). The two camps' implied conditionals are close even though their unconditional rates differ ~8x: dividing each group's AI-extinction median by its AI-catastrophe median gives 0.38/2.13 = 0.18 for XPT superforecasters and 3/12 = 0.25 for XPT domain experts. The value used here, 0.21, is the midpoint. A simulator wanting camp-specific behaviour should use 0.18 for the superforecaster prior and 0.25 for the domain-expert prior. Caveat: these are ratios of two separate medians over possibly different respondents, not a coherent individual conditional probability.

key_parameters.label: Whose elicited prior to use (0 = XPT superforecasters, 1 = XPT AI domain experts, 2 = Ord 2020 / AI-safety-researcher prior)
key_parameters.effect: This knob IS the finding — the disagreement is larger than any other quantity in the packet. Setting the annual extinction hazard directly: index 0 = XPT superforecaster median 0.38% AI-extinction by 2100 -> -ln(1-0.0038)/78 = 4.9e-5/yr; index 1 = XPT AI/nuclear/biorisk domain-expert median 3% by 2100 -> 3.9e-4/yr; index 2 = Ord's Precipice Table 6.1 figure of ~1 in 10 existential catastrophe from unaligned AI in the next 100 years -> -ln(0.9)/100 = 1.05e-3/yr. Index 2 is 21.6x index 0. The corresponding catastrophe (>=10% deaths) rates are 2.76e-4/yr (index 0) and 1.64e-3/yr (index 1); Ord gives no catastrophe-tier figure, so index 2 should reuse the index-1 catastrophe rate scaled by 10/3. Interpolate linearly in log-space between indices for intermediate values.

key_parameters.label: Year by which unaided machines outperform humans at every possible task, at 50% aggregate probability
key_parameters.effect: Capability-growth proxy, and the only capability knob in this packet with a measured downstream elasticity. Grace et al. 2023 (n=2,778) put 10% by 2027 and 50% by 2047 — 13 years earlier than the same aggregation over their 2022 survey (N=738), which gave 2060. The measured effect on risk comes from the XPT postmortem: the median superforecaster's AI-extinction-by-2100 forecast rose from 0.38% (unconditional) to 1% conditional on AGI existing by 2070, i.e. a 2.6x multiplier for AGI arriving ~30 years before the end of the horizon. As a functional form: multiply the annual hazard by 2.6^((2100 - HLMI_year)/30), clamped to >=1. Warning: this survey's timeline answers show a large framing effect — the median 50% HLMI year was 34 years out under a fixed-year framing versus 17 years out under a fixed-probability framing, a factor of two from question wording alone.

key_parameters.label: Global spending on alignment / AI-safety research, as a multiple of the present level
key_parameters.effect: NO published study estimates an elasticity of AI catastrophe probability with respect to alignment spending. There is no measured effect size in the literature and this knob's response curve is an author assumption: hazard scales as multiplier^(-beta) with beta in 0.15-0.30, so 10x spending cuts the annual rate by roughly 30-50% and 100x by 50-75%. What IS measured is demand, not supply: 70% of Grace et al.'s 2023 respondents (n=1,329) said AI safety research should be prioritised 'more' or 'much more' than at present, an increase over 2016 and only slightly over 2022; and XPT forecasters allocating a hypothetical $50bn catastrophic-risk budget in the postmortem gave 21.1% to AI risk (superforecasters, who put 25.5% into nuclear — the single case where AI did not top their list) versus 33.2% (experts). Both camps want more AI-risk spending despite disagreeing about the rate by an order of magnitude, which is itself a reportable result.

key_parameters.label: Fraction of consequential real-world actuation (grid, finance, logistics, weapons release, AI R&D) executed by AI systems without a human in the correction loop
key_parameters.effect: The mechanism above is inert at 0 — an unaligned system with no actuation cannot cause mass death. No published measurement of this quantity exists at global scale; the 0.02 current value is an author estimate and should be treated as unsourced. As a functional form, the catastrophe rate scales roughly linearly in this fraction over 0-0.3 and superlinearly above it as the number of independent human correction points falls below the number needed for any one of them to catch a failure.

'The median prediction for extremely bad outcomes, such as human extinction, was 5% (mean 9%). Over a third of participants (38%) put at least a 10% chance on extremely bad outcomes.' Table 2, three separately-worded extinction questions (2023 results): (Q1) 'future AI advances causing human extinction or similarly permanent and severe disempowerment of the human species' — N=1321; mean 16.2% (SD 23%); median 5% (IQR 19%). citations.claim: Ord's own probability for unaligned AI, and his refusal to restate it numerically four years later
citations.authors: Toby Ord
citations.venue: The Precipice: Existential Risk and the Future of Humanity (Bloomsbury), Table 6.1; restated by the author in 'The Precipice Revisited' (tobyord.com)
citations.exact_figure: 'In The Precipice, I gave my best guess probabilities for the existential risk over the next 100 years in each of these areas. These were 1 in 1,000 for Climate and for Nuclear, 1 in 30 for Pandemics and 1 in 10 for Unaligned AI.' Table 6.1's total existential risk over the next century is ~1 in 6, with ~1 in 30 for unforeseen anthropogenic risks and ~1 in 50 for other anthropogenic risks. In the 2024 revisit Ord declines to give updated numbers: 'these are all rounded off (usually to the nearest factor of 10) and none of them have moved that far.' These are one individual's subjective credences, not an elicitation of a population, and 'existential catastrophe' here includes permanent curtailment of humanity's potential, not only extinction — so it is not directly comparable to the XPT extinction criterion (population below 5,000).

citations.claim: The CAIS statement text, date and signatory composition — reported here as sociological evidence of elite coordination, not as a probability estimate
citations.authors: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
citations.venue: safe.ai / aistatement.com
citations.exact_figure: Statement, in full: 'Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.' Press release dated 30 May 2023. The signatory list is organised into exactly two categories, 'AI Scientists' and 'Other Notable Figures', and includes Turing Award winners Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio and Martin Hellman; textbook and framework authors Stuart Russell, Peter Norvig, Ian Goodfellow and Andrew Barto; the CEOs of OpenAI (Sam Altman), Google DeepMind (Demis Hassabis) and Anthropic (Dario Amodei); AI professors at Chinese universities; and non-technical figures including Bill Gates and former Estonian President Kersti Kaljulaid. IMPORTANT: neither aistatement.com nor the CAIS press release states a total signatory count anywhere on the page — the list is paginated behind a 'Show more' control. Any specific total (the widely repeated '350+' and '700+' figures) could not be verified against a primary source in this session and is therefore NOT asserted here. The statement carries no probability, no time horizon and no mechanism; it is a coordination artefact, and cannot be converted into a rate.

citations.claim: The XPT persuasion sub-study: prolonged, incentivised, structured debate between the two camps moved neither, which is why the disagreement should be modelled as a standing parameter rather than as noise awaiting resolution
citations.authors: Josh Rosenberg, Ezra Karger, Avital Morris, Molly Hickman, Rose Hadshar, Zachary Jacobs, Philip E. Tetlock
citations.venue: Forecasting Research Institute, 'Roots of Disagreement on AI Risk' (11 March 2024)
citations.exact_figure: n=22 (concerned group: 11 participants, all domain experts; skeptic group: 11, comprising 9 superforecasters and 2 domain experts), studied over 8 weeks in April-May 2023, with median engagement of 80 hours (skeptics) and 31 hours (concerned). Median forecast of existential catastrophe by 2100 fell from 25% to 20% in the concerned group and moved from 0.10% to 0.12% in the skeptic group — a gap of more than two orders of magnitude that structured persuasion did not close. Existential catastrophe was defined as humanity going extinct or experiencing 'unrecoverable collapse' (sustained global GDP below $1 trillion annually, or human population below 1 million, for a million years, beginning before 2100). The parent XPT report records the same result at tournament scale: 'Few minds were changed during the XPT, even among the most active participants, and despite monetary incentives for persuading others.'

hazards.uncertainty_notes:
The disagreement IS the result, and it is not a disagreement about severity — it is a disagreement about rate. Divide each XPT group's AI-extinction median by its AI-catastrophe median and the implied conditional probability of extinction given catastrophe is 0.18 (superforecasters) and 0.25 (domain experts): nearly the same. But the unconditional rates differ by a factor of 8 (catastrophe) and 8 (extinction), and Ord's own credence sits another 3.3x above the domain experts. A simulator that averages these camps is reporting a number no participant holds.

Where this packet is weakest, in the order a serious critic would attack it:
(1) The annualisation is a fiction. Every source gives a by-2100 cumulative probability; -ln(1-p)/78 assumes a constant hazard, and both camps explicitly do not believe that. The near-term rate is probably overstated several-fold and the 2070-2100 rate understated.
(2) Elicitation format moves these numbers by six orders of magnitude. The XPT's own parallel public survey (912 college graduates) gave a 2% median for AI-caused extinction by 2100 when asked for a percentage, and a median of 1 in 30 MILLION for the same event when asked to fill in X in '1-in-X', after being shown reference classes such as a 1-in-300,000 lifetime chance of being killed by lightning. Total extinction went from 5% to 1 in 15 million; catastrophe from 11.56% to 1 in 2,500. This was the public, not the forecasters, but it is the single most damning methodological fact in this literature and nobody has shown the expert samples are immune.
(3) Question wording moves the expert numbers by 2x. Grace et al. asked three near-identical extinction questions of disjoint subsamples and got medians of 5%, 10% and 5%; the 'human inability to control' framing reliably doubles the 'future AI advances' framing. Their HLMI timelines moved by a factor of two on fixed-year versus fixed-probability framing.
(4) Selection. Grace et al.'s response rate is 15% (2,778 of 18,459 functioning addresses); the authors defend it as normal for a >20,000-person invitation list and report finding no evidence of strong participation bias, but a survey about AI risk sent to AI researchers has an obvious differential-interest problem that no analysis inside the survey can fully rule out. The XPT expert sample is worse in a different way: 42% of experts (versus 9% of superforecasters) reported having attended an Effective Altruism meetup, and 44% of experts spent more than 200 hours on existential-risk work in the prior year versus 11% of superforecasters. The 'experts' are, in substantial part, a community with a prior commitment to the proposition being estimated. Symmetrically, superforecaster status was earned on short-horizon geopolitical questions with feedback, and there is no evidence it transfers to 78-year questions that can never be scored in a forecaster's lifetime; the XPT report states this counter-argument itself.
(5) Aggregation choice changes the answer by 4x within a single group. Table 4 of the XPT: AI domain experts' AI-extinction risk is 3% by median but 13.61% by arithmetic mean and 1.33% by geometric mean of odds. Reporting 'the expert estimate' as a single number conceals this.
(6) n=29 AI experts. That is the actual sample behind the 3% figure everyone quotes.
(7) Ord's 1 in 10 is one person's credence, published as a round number, and the author declined to update it numerically in 2024. It should never be treated as an elicitation result.
(8) The severity-tier split between 'major catastrophe' and 'collapse' (0.52 / 0.22 / 0.05 / 0.21) is an AUTHOR-ESTIMATE. No published source decomposes AI catastrophe severity above the >=10%-deaths threshold; only the extinction/catastrophe ratio is data-derived, and even that is a ratio of two independent medians rather than a coherent individual conditional.
(9) The XPT catastrophe question does not separate loss of control from deliberate misuse. This hazard and 'ai-enabled-misuse' therefore double-count; a simulator should not sum them.
(10) The CAIS statement carries no number and cannot be converted into one. Its evidential content is that a large set of people with direct technical knowledge and, in several cases, strong commercial incentives to say the opposite were willing to put their names to the extinction framing. A critic will note the reverse reading with equal force — that a statement costing nothing to sign, from parties who benefit from their products being described as world-historically powerful, is weak evidence about the world and strong evidence about an industry's positioning. Both readings are available and neither is quantitative. This packet does not assert a signatory count, because no primary page states one.

hazards.name: AI-enabled misuse (bioweapon design assistance, autonomous weapons, mass persuasion, authoritarian entrenchment)
hazards.one_line: Humans deliberately use AI systems to lower the capability barrier to mass-casualty attack, to remove humans from lethal decision loops, or to make populations permanently uncontestable.
hazards.mechanism: Four distinct near-term mechanisms with different kill chains, sharing only the tool. (a) Bioweapon design assistance: the barrier to a mass-casualty biological attack has never been information, it has been tacit laboratory skill, agent acquisition and aerosolisation; the concern is that a sufficiently capable model collapses the protocol-troubleshooting portion of that barrier, moving a scenario from state-scale to small-group-scale. Death then arrives through an engineered pathogen and, above a few percent mortality, through the collapse of health systems and food distribution rather than through the pathogen alone. (b) Autonomous weapons: the mechanism is not a robot uprising but the removal of the human deliberation that currently caps engagement rate and escalation speed — automated systems on both sides of a confrontation can complete an escalation cycle faster than any political process can interrupt it, with nuclear-armed states as the terminal case. (c) Mass persuasion: personalised, conversational, cheap argument at population scale degrades the shared factual substrate a society needs to notice and respond to any of the other hazards in this packet; it kills nobody directly and raises every other hazard's severity by degrading the response. (d) Authoritarian entrenchment: comprehensive monitoring plus predictive policing removes the coordination window that historically ends bad regimes, converting a recoverable political failure into a permanent one — the only pathway here that is terminal without being lethal.

annual_probability.event_definition: A mass-casualty event (>=1,000 deaths) in which AI assistance was materially causal to the perpetrator's capability — that is, the attack would not have been feasible for that actor without it. THIS IS AN AUTHOR ESTIMATE AND IS NOT DRAWN FROM ANY PUBLISHED FIGURE. No such event has occurred. The observed count is 0 over roughly four years of widely available frontier LLMs, which places essentially no upper constraint (a zero-count over 4 years bounds the rate only below ~0.75/yr at 95%). The estimate is anchored downward by the RAND red-team null result and upward by the fact that frontier developers have already begun activating heightened safeguards on the strength of internal evaluations they will not fully publish. Treat the range as spanning two and a half orders of magnitude because that is genuinely the state of knowledge.
annual_probability.trend: Rising, and this is the one place in the packet where the trend is better evidenced than the level. RAND (January 2024) found no measurable uplift from the then-current LLM generation. Sixteen months later (22 May 2025) Anthropic activated its ASL-3 CBRN deployment and security standard for Claude Opus 4, stating it had 'not yet determined whether Claude Opus 4 has definitively passed the Capabilities Threshold that requires ASL-3 protections' and was acting 'as a precautionary and provisional action' in light of continued improvements in CBRN-related knowledge and capabilities. The direction of travel between those two data points is unambiguous; the magnitude is not measured by either.

severity_tiers.label: Contained incident
severity_tiers.description: 1,000 to ~100,000 deaths: a single successful attack, a localised outbreak, or an autonomous-weapons engagement gone wrong. Contained by conventional public-health or military response. The dominant real-world consequence is regulatory — this is the tier that produces the international agreement, the export controls, and the mandatory pre-deployment evaluation regime.

severity_tiers.label: Regional mass-casualty event or limited pandemic
severity_tiers.description: 0.5-5% of world population. An engineered agent escapes containment regionally, or an automated escalation produces a conventional war with a mass-casualty exchange. Health systems in affected regions fail; global supply chains are disrupted but not broken.

severity_tiers.label: Global catastrophe
severity_tiers.description: >=10% of world population within five years — the XPT catastrophe threshold. An engineered pathogen with both high transmissibility and high case-fatality, or a nuclear exchange reached through an automated escalation cycle. Most of the deaths above the direct toll come from the failure of food and medical distribution in the following two growing seasons.

severity_tiers.label: Terminal release
severity_tiers.description: An engineered agent optimised simultaneously for transmissibility, latency and lethality — the combination natural selection does not produce because it is not adaptive for the pathogen. Population falls below the threshold for maintaining any industrial society and does not recover.

key_parameters.label: Viability of a biological-attack plan produced with frontier-LLM assistance, relative to internet access alone
key_parameters.effect: 1.0 is the measured value, not an assumption: RAND's red-team study found 'no statistically significant difference in the viability of plans generated with or without LLM assistance,' concluding that 'biological weapon attack planning currently lies beyond the capability frontier of LLMs as assistive tools.' The rate of AI-materially-causal bio events should be modelled as scaling with the number of actors for whom the capability barrier is actually removed, which is approximately zero while this ratio is 1.0 and rises sharply once it exceeds the threshold separating a motivated small group from a state programme. Two hard caveats the RAND authors state themselves: the study 'did not measure the distance between the existing LLM capability frontier and the knowledge needed for biological weapon attack planning' — so it is a null result, not a safety margin — and they would want to increase sensitivity by testing more LLMs and involving more researchers. A null on an underpowered test is not evidence of absence.

key_parameters.label: Fraction of lethal engagements executed with no operator in the decision loop
key_parameters.effect: 0.0 is the defensible current value, and the reason is a careful reading of the only documented case. The UN Panel of Experts on Libya (S/2021/229, March 2021, para. 63) reported that STM Kargu-2 loitering munitions and other systems 'were programmed to attack targets without requiring data connectivity between the operator and the munition: in effect, a true fire, forget and find capability,' and (para. 64) that retreating Haftar-affiliated forces 'were subject to continual harassment from the unmanned combat aerial vehicles and lethal autonomous weapons systems' and 'suffered significant casualties.' The report does NOT confirm that any engagement was executed autonomously, nor that the systems killed anyone while unsupervised. The widely repeated claim of a 'first autonomous kill' is not supported by the primary document. Effect on the model: escalation-driven conflict rate scales roughly with this fraction times the number of adversary pairs whose systems can interact; the qualitative change is that above ~0.1 the escalation cycle time drops below human political decision time, which is a threshold, not a slope.

key_parameters.label: Increase in odds of opinion change when the interlocutor is GPT-4 with sociodemographic data on the subject, versus a human
key_parameters.effect: Measured in a pre-registered randomised controlled trial: participants debating GPT-4 with access to their personal information had 81.7% higher odds of increased agreement with their opponent than participants debating humans (p < 0.01, N=820 unique participants). Without personalisation GPT-4 still outperformed humans but the effect was smaller and not statistically significant (p = 0.31) — personalisation, not raw model quality, is what carries the effect. This knob does not enter the death rate directly. Model it as a multiplier on the response-failure term of every other hazard in the packet: an epistemically degraded population detects and acts on a novel hazard more slowly. There is NO published elasticity linking persuasion effect size to collective-response failure, so the mapping from this knob to any mortality figure is an author assumption. The researcher-concern signal is separately measured: 86% of Grace et al.'s 2023 respondents (n=1,345) rated 'spread of false information e.g. deepfakes' as worthy of substantial or extreme concern, and 79% rated 'manipulation of large-scale public opinion trends' — the two highest-ranked of eleven scenarios.

key_parameters.label: Share of published AI researchers rating 'authoritarian rulers using AI to control their populations' as worthy of substantial or extreme concern
key_parameters.effect: 73% (Grace et al. 2023, n=1,345), tied with 'AI letting dangerous groups make powerful tools (e.g. engineered viruses)' also at 73%, and behind only deepfakes (86%) and opinion manipulation (79%); every one of the eleven scenarios cleared 30%. BE CLEAR ABOUT WHAT THIS IS: a measure of expert concern, not a measure of adoption, and not a rate. It is included as a knob because no published figure exists for the quantity a simulator actually wants — the share of world population under governments running AI-enabled population monitoring — and substituting a concern percentage for an adoption percentage would be exactly the sleight of hand this packet is meant to avoid. Use it as a scenario selector, not as a coefficient. The entrenchment pathway is the only one in this hazard that is terminal without being lethal, and it maps onto the 'permanent disempowerment without extinction' tier of the unaligned-ai hazard rather than onto any tier here.

citations.claim: Frontier LLMs as of the 2023-24 generation gave no measurable uplift in biological attack planning
citations.authors: Christopher A. Mouton, Caleb Lucas, Ella Guest
citations.venue: RAND Corporation, report RR-A2977-2, doi 10.7249/RRA2977-2, published 25 January 2024, 24 pp. (final results; preceded by RR-A2977-1, 16 October 2023)
citations.exact_figure: 'The findings indicate that using the existing generation of LLMs did not measurably change the operational risk of such an attack.' Key takeaways, verbatim: 'This research involving multiple LLMs indicates that biological weapon attack planning currently lies beyond the capability frontier of LLMs as assistive tools. The authors found no statistically significant difference in the viability of plans generated with or without LLM assistance.' And, as a stated limitation: 'This research did not measure the distance between the existing LLM capability frontier and the knowledge needed for biological weapon attack planning.' Design: an expert exercise in which teams role-playing malign non-state actors were assigned realistic scenarios and tasked with planning a biological attack; some teams had an LLM plus the internet, others the internet only. The authors note they would want to 'increase the sensitivity of these tests by expanding the number of LLMs tested, involving more researchers, and removing unhelpful sources of variability.'

citations.claim: A frontier developer activated heightened CBRN safeguards in 2025 without having confirmed the capability threshold was crossed — evidence of trend direction, and of the limits of public evidence
citations.authors: Anthropic
citations.venue: Anthropic, 'Activating AI Safety Level 3 Protections', 22 May 2025
citations.exact_figure: 'We have not yet determined whether Claude Opus 4 has definitively passed the Capabilities Threshold that requires ASL-3 protections.' The model was deployed under the ASL-3 Deployment and Security Standard 'as a precautionary and provisional action'; the stated reason is continued improvements in CBRN-related knowledge and capabilities making the risk impossible to rule out, with initial focus on biological weapons. Claude Sonnet 4 was kept at the ASL-2 standard. This is a first-party statement by an interested developer, published without the underlying evaluation data, and should be treated as an indicator of direction rather than as a measurement of uplift.

citations.claim: The only documented battlefield use of a loitering munition described by the UN as a lethal autonomous weapons system — and what the primary document does and does not say
citations.authors: UN Panel of Experts on Libya, Letter dated 8 March 2021 to the President of the Security Council, UN doc S/2021/229 (reproduced in the ICRC 'How does law protect in war?' online casebook)
citations.venue: United Nations Security Council / ICRC casebook
citations.exact_figure: Para. 63: 'The lethal autonomous weapons systems were programmed to attack targets without requiring data connectivity between the operator and the munition: in effect, a true "fire, forget and find" capability.' Para. 64 records that retreating Haftar Affiliated Forces 'were subject to continual harassment from the unmanned combat aerial vehicles and lethal autonomous weapons systems' and 'suffered significant casualties.' The system named is the STM Kargu-2. CRITICAL READING: the report attributes a capability, not an executed autonomous engagement. It does not state that the system selected or engaged a human target without operator involvement, and does not attribute any specific death to autonomous operation. The frequently repeated 'first autonomous kill in history' framing is not supported by the primary text.

citations.claim: How published AI researchers rank the near-term misuse mechanisms against each other
citations.authors: Katja Grace, Harlan Stewart, Julia Fabienne Sandkühler, Stephen Thomas, Ben Weinstein-Raun, Jan Brauner, Richard C. Korzekwa
citations.venue: arXiv:2401.02843; Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research vol. 84 (2025), doi 10.1613/jair.1.19087
citations.exact_figure: Respondents (n=1,345) were asked about eleven potentially concerning AI scenarios. 'Each scenario was considered worthy of either substantial or extreme concern by more than 30% of respondents.' Ranked by the share rating substantial or extreme concern: spread of false information e.g. deepfakes 86%; manipulation of large-scale public opinion trends 79%; AI letting dangerous groups make powerful tools (e.g. engineered viruses) 73%; authoritarian rulers using AI to control their populations 73%; AI systems worsening economic inequality (also among the top five). Separately, on the meta-question 'To what extent do you think people's concerns about future risks from AI are due to misunderstandings of AI research?' (n=671): 10.7% 'Almost entirely', 44% 'To a large extent', 29.1% 'Somewhat', 14.6% 'Not much', 1.6% 'Hardly at all' — i.e. a majority of AI researchers think public concern is substantially rooted in misunderstanding, while a majority of the same population assigns >=5% to extinction-level outcomes. Both facts are in the same survey.

cascades_into: unaligned-ai: the same capability frontier and the same deployment surface produce both; the XPT catastrophe question does not separate them, so a simulator must not sum the two hazards' rates
engineered-pandemic: this is the dominant sub-mechanism, and the AI contribution is a multiplier on the number of actors capable of executing a release rather than an independent cause

nuclear-war: automated escalation compresses the decision cycle below the time required for political de-escalation, raising the conditional probability of exchange given a crisis rather than the crisis rate itself
great-power-conflict: cheap autonomous systems lower the materiel and casualty cost of initiating conflict, and mass persuasion raises the domestic feasibility of sustaining one

systemic-epistemic-failure: mass persuasion and information pollution degrade the collective detection-and-response capacity that every other hazard's mitigation depends on — this is a severity multiplier on the whole packet, not a separate kill mechanism
hazards.uncertainty_notes:
The honest headline: THE ANNUAL PROBABILITY IN THIS HAZARD IS AN AUTHOR ESTIMATE, NOT A PUBLISHED FIGURE. No source consulted publishes a rate for AI-materially-causal mass-casualty attacks, and the observed count is zero, so the number is a prior with a two-and-a-half-order-of-magnitude range, not a measurement. It should be labelled as such wherever a simulator surfaces it, and it should not be presented alongside the XPT and Grace figures as if it had the same standing.

What IS well evidenced here is the mechanism inventory and the direction of travel; what is not evidenced is any rate.

Specific attack surfaces a critic will use:
(1) The RAND null is underpowered by its own authors' admission, and it measures the wrong thing for forecasting: it tested the 2023-24 model generation, and explicitly did not measure the gap between that frontier and the capability that would matter. Citing it as reassurance is a misreading; citing it as a base rate is the correct use.
(2) The counterweight to RAND is first-party and unaudited. Anthropic's ASL-3 activation is a company's statement about its own product, published without the evaluation data, by an organisation with a commercial interest in its models being understood as powerful. It is genuine evidence of what an internal evaluation showed, and it is also marketing-adjacent. Both are true.
(3) The autonomous-weapons literature is contaminated by a widely repeated claim the primary document does not make. S/2021/229 describes a capability, not a confirmed autonomous engagement, and several secondary sources have converted this into 'the first autonomous kill'. Any model calibrated on that claim is calibrated on an artefact of press coverage.
(4) The persuasion result is a real, pre-registered RCT with a real effect, on a short online debate with sociodemographic personalisation, over topics of varying opinion strength. Generalising an 81.7% odds increase in that setting to population-scale epistemic degradation is a leap the paper does not make and this packet does not have evidence for. The link from persuasion effect size to any mortality figure is entirely an author assumption.
(5) The authoritarian-entrenchment pathway has the weakest quantitative footing of the four and the strongest claim to being terminal. The knob offered is a measure of researcher concern, not of adoption, because no adoption figure was located; a simulator that treats 73% as a deployment share is making an error this packet is explicitly trying to prevent.
(6) The severity tier probabilities (0.80 / 0.16 / 0.035 / 0.005) are author estimates with no source. They encode the judgement that most successful misuse events are contained and that the jump to a >=10%-mortality event requires an agent with a transmissibility-lethality combination that natural selection does not favour — which is an argument, not a measurement.
(7) Overlap with 'unaligned-ai' is real and unresolved. The XPT's 2.13%/12% AI-catastrophe figures cover misuse and loss of control together. If a simulator uses that rate for the unaligned-ai hazard and then adds this hazard's rate on top, it is double-counting. The correct treatment is either to use this hazard as a decomposition of the unaligned-ai rate, or to run them as alternative framings of the same event.

hazards.name: Biosphere degradation: pollinator, soil, aquifer and fishery loss
hazards.one_line: The chronic erosion of the biological and physical capital that agriculture stands on, which so far lowers the system's buffer against shocks rather than lowering output.
hazards.mechanism: Nothing in biosphere degradation kills people directly, and any model in which it does is wrong on the observed record. It works by thinning the stock of free inputs agriculture draws on: animal pollination underwrites 35% of global production volume, though only 13 of 107 crops assessed by Klein et al. lose 90% or more without pollinators and none of those are the wind- or self-pollinated cereals that supply most calories; conventional tillage removes topsoil at roughly 1 mm/yr against soil production one to two orders of magnitude slower; irrigation is mining stored groundwater that does not recharge on human timescales (286.4 million acre-feet gone from the High Plains aquifer, about 9% of recoverable storage, with an area-weighted decline of 16.5 ft); and marine capture has fallen from 90% of assessed stocks fished within biologically sustainable levels in 1974 to 62.4% by 2023. Every one of these losses is compensable in the short run by more synthetic nitrogen, more pumping energy, more land and more fishing effort, which is exactly why world agricultural output rose nearly fourfold between 1961 and 2020 on only 7.6% more land while output per capita rose 53%. The compensations are bought with inputs, and the inputs are concentrated: 48% of the world population is fed on Haber-Bosch nitrogen, and 68% of phosphate rock reserves sit in a single country. So the causal chain to mass death runs entirely through a later shock: degradation converts a system with slack into a system already running at the edge of its substitutes, so that when a harvest failure arrives the floor it falls onto is lower and the compensating levers are already pulled. Deaths, when they come, are famine deaths and infectious-disease deaths in malnourished import-dependent populations, not deaths from the loss of a bee.

annual_probability.event_definition: Onset in a given year of a further discrete degradation step, defined as a 5-percentage-point reduction in attainable global crop calorie supply relative to a no-degradation counterfactual, sustained for at least 10 years. This is NOT the probability of any deaths; it is the probability of the buffer-reducing event that other hazards in this packet draw on.
annual_probability.trend: Rising in the aggregate but decelerating in several components. Fish stock sustainability fell ~0.57 pp/yr on average from 1974 to 2023 and is still falling (64.5% to 62.4% between the 2024 and 2026 SOFIA assessments). HANPP rose from 15.7% to 23.5% of potential natural NPP between 1950 and 2020 (~0.11 pp/yr). Against this, stratospheric ozone is recovering (284.6 DU vs a 290 DU preindustrial base) and no-till adoption cuts erosion by roughly an order of magnitude where adopted, so the trend is a policy variable, not a physical constant.

severity_tiers.label: Absorbed by inputs
severity_tiers.description: The degradation step is fully offset by fertiliser, irrigation energy, managed pollination, and yield genetics, exactly as every step of the last sixty years has been. Global cereal yields and per-capita output keep rising. Excess mortality is confined to micronutrient-deficiency disease in populations losing access to pollinator-dependent fruits, nuts and vegetables and to small-scale fish protein — a nutrition-quality effect, not a calorie effect.

severity_tiers.label: Regionally binding
severity_tiers.description: Specific regions cross their local thresholds rather than the global aggregate moving. High Plains irrigated area converts to dryland as saturated thickness falls below pumping viability; North China Plain deep-aquifer districts retire cropland; thin-soil tropical uplands lose their A horizon; small-scale fisheries collapse. Those regions flip from net exporters to net importers, tightening world trade in normal years and leaving less slack for a bad one.

severity_tiers.label: Yield ceiling falls
severity_tiers.description: Global attainable yield growth turns negative for a decade despite maximal input use — the input treadmill stops paying. Total factor productivity growth, which already fell from 1.99%/yr (2001-10) to 1.12%/yr (2011-20), goes to zero or below. Chronic import dependence in low-income countries becomes structural and the reserve buffer for a food-system shock is spent in normal years rather than held for a bad one.

key_parameters.label: Share of global production volume from pollinator-dependent crops
key_parameters.effect: Klein et al. 2007 give 35% of global production volume from crops that depend on animal pollination, 60% from crops that do not, 5% unevaluated. Dependence is graded, not binary: of 107 crops, 13 lose >=90% without pollinators, 30 lose 40-90%, 27 lose 10-40%, 21 lose 0-10%, 7 show no increase. A defensible total-collapse loss is L = sum_c (share_c x dependence_c), which lands around 5-8% of global production volume, and near ZERO for staple cereal calories since wheat, rice and maize are wind- or self-pollinated. Wire this knob to micronutrient and fruit/nut/oilseed availability, not to the calorie aggregate; dCalories/dP is approximately 0 while dVitaminA/dP is strongly negative.

key_parameters.label: Net soil erosion rate on conventionally tilled cropland
key_parameters.effect: Montgomery 2007: conventionally plowed fields erode at rates 1-2 orders of magnitude greater than soil production, averaging about 1 mm/yr net, against USDA tolerable-loss (T) values of 0.4-1.0 mm/yr. With roughly 0.3 m of A horizon, time to exhaustion is approximately 300 mm / (E - F) years, where F, soil production, is about 0.01-0.1 mm/yr: about 300 years at E = 1.0 mm/yr, about 3000 years at no-till E = 0.1 mm/yr. Yield penalty is roughly linear in remaining topsoil depth once below about 0.2 m. This is a slow ramp on the yield ceiling with a centennial time constant, not a cliff, and it is the parameter most responsive to management. Borrelli et al. 2017 put the global flux at 35.9 Pg/yr in 2012, up 2.5% on land-use change.

key_parameters.label: Human appropriation of net primary production
key_parameters.effect: Richardson et al. 2023 set the functional-biosphere-integrity boundary at HANPP < 10% of preindustrial Holocene mean NPP (55.9 Gt C/yr, stable to within +/- 1.1 Gt C/yr at 2 sigma), with the high-risk zone above 20%; the current value is 30%, or 16.8 Gt C/yr in 2020. Each additional percentage point removes about 0.56 Gt C/yr from ecosystem energy flow. Treat as a monotone reducer of ecosystem-service resilience (pest regulation, pollination, nutrient cycling) rather than as a direct yield term — the paper deliberately gives no HANPP-to-yield transfer function, and inventing one would be the most likely place for a simulator to fabricate doom.

key_parameters.label: Share of aquifer recoverable storage drained since predevelopment (High Plains as index basin)
key_parameters.effect: USGS: High Plains recoverable storage was about 2.91 billion acre-feet in 2019 after a decline of about 286.4 million acre-feet since predevelopment (about 9% gone), area-weighted water-level change -16.5 ft, individual wells ranging from +86 ft to -265 ft. The basin mean is the wrong variable because depletion is spatially extreme: the operative quantity is the share of irrigated area that has crossed its local saturated-thickness pumping threshold. Model as a one-way ratchet converting irrigated to dryland cropland, roughly 1-2 pp of basin irrigated area lost per pp of storage lost, with a 30-60% yield drop on conversion. North China Plain behaves similarly at 2.2 +/- 0.3 cm/yr of depletion (8.3 +/- 1.1 km3/yr) over 2003-2010.

key_parameters.label: Single-country share of world phosphate rock reserves
key_parameters.effect: USGS 2025: Morocco holds 50 billion metric tons of phosphate rock, an estimated 68% of world reserves, while supplying an estimated 15% of 2024 production (China is the largest producer). Phosphorus has no substitute and no synthetic route. Concentration does not change long-run resource life; it sets the probability and depth of a price or embargo shock. A Morocco supply interruption removes about 15% of annual flow immediately and caps long-run supply expansion. Couple this knob to the fertiliser-supply knob of the food-shock hazard rather than to yields directly — phosphorus acts through a multi-year soil-P drawdown, not within one season the way nitrogen does. Note separately that the phosphorus planetary boundary is already transgressed at 22.6 Tg P/yr against a boundary of 11 Tg P/yr: the problem is simultaneously oversupply into water and undersupply security on land.

citations.authors: Alexandra-Maria Klein, Bernard E. Vaissiere, James H. Cane, Ingolf Steffan-Dewenter, Saul A. Cunningham, Claire Kremen, Teja Tscharntke

Ord states these should be treated as representing the right order of magnitude, each potentially a factor of 3 higher or lower.

hazards.uncertainty_notes: THE ANNUAL PROBABILITY IS AN AUTHOR ESTIMATE AND IS THE WEAKEST NUMBER IN THIS ENTRY. No published source gives a per-year probability for a composite 'biosphere degradation step', because degradation is a trend rather than a Poisson event; I constructed 3%/yr (roughly one 5-pp step per 20-40 years) by projecting four independently measured rates — HANPP +0.11 pp/yr, fish-stock sustainability -0.57 pp/yr, terrestrial insect abundance -0.92 to -1.11%/yr, High Plains storage -9% over ~70 years. A critic should attack that aggregation directly: the four indicators are not commensurable, and summing them into a single 'attainable calorie supply' fraction is my construction, not anyone's finding. SECOND, the pollinator-to-calorie link is routinely overstated in popular treatments and I have deliberately not used the '35% of food' framing as a calorie figure: Klein's 35% is production VOLUME, dominated by fruits, vegetables and oilseeds, and the staple cereals supplying most calories are wind- or self-pollinated. I could not retrieve this session a published estimate of mortality attributable to pollinator loss (Smith et al. 2015, Lancet, is the relevant paper and I did not fetch it); the 0.0005 deaths_fraction in tier 1 is therefore an author estimate standing in for that unretrieved figure. THIRD, the insect-decline literature is genuinely contested and I have represented both sides: Hallmann's 76%/82% comes from a design in which 59% of locations were sampled in a single year, and van Klink's global meta-analysis puts terrestrial decline at roughly one-tenth the Krefeld rate while finding freshwater insects INCREASING — and van Klink is itself the subject of a formal Comment in Science alleging errors and biases, with a published Response. Any simulator using '75% of insects gone' as a global parameter is using a local, contested figure as a planetary one. FOURTH, the planetary-boundaries framework quantifies transgression, not consequence: Richardson et al. explicitly decline to supply a HANPP-to-yield transfer function, and inventing one is the most likely route by which a model would manufacture doom that the evidence does not support. FIFTH, the High Plains figures are for one basin and the basin mean badly understates the local picture (wells range +86 ft to -265 ft); I did not retrieve a global groundwater-depletion total this session. SIXTH, note the direction-of-error asymmetry: the entire observed record runs the other way — output per capita up 53% since 1961 — so the burden of proof on any lethal coefficient here is high, and I have set no terminal tier because there is no evidential basis for one on a century timescale.
cascades_into: global-food-system-shock-multi-breadbasket-failure: this is the primary and arguably the only important effect — degradation lowers the yield floor a shock falls onto and pre-spends the input substitutions (fertiliser, pumping, land, fishing effort) that would otherwise absorb it, converting a survivable production dip into a deficit reserves cannot cover

conflict-and-state-fragility: regionally binding water and soil limits produce internal displacement and transboundary water disputes that raise the baseline rate of state failure in already-fragile food-importing states

hazards.name: Global food-system shock via multi-breadbasket failure
hazards.one_line: Simultaneous climate-driven harvest failure in several of the handful of regions that supply most traded grain, converted into famine by export restriction and reserve inaccessibility rather than by the calorie deficit itself.
hazards.mechanism: A multi-breadbasket failure is a single-year, weather-driven collapse of yields in several of the small number of regions that supply most internationally traded grain — US maize, Black Sea and Australian wheat, South Asian rice, Southern Cone soy — driven by the correlated atmospheric patterns (ENSO phases, persistent blocking, jet-stream waveguide states) that can hit them in the same season. The physical deficit is survivable on its face: a 10% global cereal shortfall is about 36 days of world consumption, and carry-over stocks stand at 31.6% of use, roughly 115 days. What kills is the policy response and the distribution of who eats. Exporters insulate their domestic markets: Martin and Anderson attribute 45% of the 2006-08 rise in world rice prices and 30% of the rise in wheat prices to insulating trade behaviour, which is self-cancelling on average across countries while converting a moderate global shortfall into an extreme price shock for the countries that must import. Poor import-dependent households then buy fewer calories and cheaper, less nutritious calories; child wasting and stunting rise; and infectious-disease case-fatality rises in an undernourished population. In states already fragile, the price shock plus the fiscal shock of import subsidies produces unrest and conflict, which disrupts the following season's planting and turns a one-year event into a multi-year one. Almost every death is a famine or epidemic death in a low-income food-deficit importer, months to years after the harvest that failed, and geographically nowhere near the breadbasket that failed.

annual_probability.event_definition: A single-year decline of >=10% in global cereal production relative to the preceding three-year mean, arising from simultaneous climate-driven yield failure in three or more major breadbasket regions. Excludes nuclear-winter and volcanic-winter causes, which belong to their own hazard entries and have their own (much larger) severity distributions. This is the probability the SHOCK occurs, not the probability anyone dies from it.
annual_probability.trend: Rising, and this is the best-evidenced trend in the packet. Gaupp et al. find the annual probability of ALL studied breadbaskets simultaneously experiencing climate risk rose from 0.3% to 1.2% for wheat, 0.8% to 1.1% for maize and 1.7% to 2.0% for soybean between 1967-1990 and 1991-2012 — a fourfold rise for wheat within the observational record. Under warming, modelled multiple-breadbasket-failure risk for maize rises from 6% to 40% at 1.5 C and 54% at 2 C. Cottrell et al. independently find 226 food production shocks across 134 nations over 53 years with increasing frequency across all sectors. Countervailing: the buffer trend is favourable, with stock-to-use at 31.6% and 2026/27 the second-largest harvest on record.

severity_tiers.label: Price spike, reserves hold
severity_tiers.description: Reserves are drawn down, world cereal prices roughly double for 12-24 months, and the food-insecure population rises by tens to low hundreds of millions — the 2007-08 and 2010-11 pattern, in which no measurable global excess-mortality signal appeared. Trade stays largely open, the deficit is spread across importers, and the next harvest closes it.

severity_tiers.label: Export-restriction cascade
severity_tiers.description: Major exporters ban or tax exports, which is individually rational and collectively catastrophic: the physically available grain exists but does not move. Prices in import-dependent countries rise multiples above the world fundamental (rice rose 117-149% in Q1 2008 on restrictions plus panic buying by importers). Regional famines occur in low-income food-deficit importers and in conflict-affected states; urban unrest and government instability follow the price series with a lag of months.

severity_tiers.label: Multi-year deficit, reserves exhausted
severity_tiers.description: The shock repeats or persists for three or more seasons — the correlated-climate case, or a first-year failure followed by conflict-driven planting failure. Accessible stocks are gone by year two; humanitarian systems are overwhelmed; famine becomes continental rather than national. Livestock herds are slaughtered for grain-sparing, removing the protein base for a decade. Industrial capacity is not destroyed but is diverted, and recovery is limited by rebuilding herds, seed stocks and rural labour.

severity_tiers.label: Compound collapse
severity_tiers.description: Harvest failure coincides with a trade shutdown AND an interruption of synthetic nitrogen or phosphate supply for three or more consecutive seasons — the case where the buffer built by hazard 1's degradation has already been spent. Because roughly 48% of the world population is fed on Haber-Bosch nitrogen and the effect hits the entire planted area at once rather than one region, the loss is not regional and not bufferable by stocks. Deaths approach the scale modelled for a regional nuclear winter (>2 billion in Xia et al.'s India-Pakistan case), but seed stock, land, knowledge and most industrial capacity survive, so recovery is a matter of decades rather than never.

key_parameters.label: World cereal carry-over stocks expressed as days of consumption
key_parameters.effect: FAO Cereal Supply and Demand Brief, 4 September 2026: world cereal stock-to-use ratio 31.6% for 2026/27 (ending stocks 947.2 Mt against utilization 2,965 Mt), which is 0.316 x 365 = 115 days. A shortfall of fraction f removes 365f days of supply, so the uncovered deficit is D = max(0, 365f - R x a) days, where R is reserve days and a is the ACCESSIBLE fraction of world stocks. At f = 0.10 (36.5 days) the deficit is fully covered for any a > 0.32; at f = 0.25 (91 days) only for a > 0.79. Price response is convex once D > 0, roughly dP/P proportional to D^1.5 to D^2. The accessible fraction a is the single largest uncertainty in this whole entry: a large share of world stocks is held as strategic reserve by one country and does not enter international trade, so the effective R for an importer is far below 115 days. I could not retrieve a figure for that share this session — treat a as a free parameter in [0.3, 0.8] and note that the model is most sensitive to it.

key_parameters.label: Share of a world price rise attributable to insulating trade policy
key_parameters.effect: Martin and Anderson: 'the analysis suggests that 45 percent of the increase in rice prices in 2006-08, and 30 percent of the increase in wheat prices, was due to insulating behavior.' Insulation is a pure collective-action failure — ineffective on average at stabilising domestic prices while increasing world price volatility. Model as a multiplicative amplifier on the fundamental price move: P_world = P_fundamental / (1 - s), so s = 0.30 gives x1.43 and s = 0.45 gives x1.82. Let s rise endogenously with the uncovered deficit D from the reserve knob, since restrictions are triggered by domestic price alarm rather than by global scarcity. Thinly traded staples insulate worse than thickly traded ones: developing countries account for 97% of world rice consumption but only 73% of wheat, which is why rice showed the higher insulation share and why rice is the correct worst case.

key_parameters.label: Crop commodities supplying the top 90% of global calories, protein, fat and weight
key_parameters.effect: Khoury et al.: across 152 countries and 1961-2009, '50 of the measured crop commodities currently contribute to the top 90% of calories, protein, fat, and weight globally', and 'homogeneity increased by 16.7%, as measured by the mean change in similarity between each country and the global standard composition'. Diversity acts on the COVARIANCE of the calorie aggregate, not its mean. With n effectively independent staples of comparable share, the variance of aggregate supply scales roughly as 1/n, so halving n roughly doubles the variance of the global calorie aggregate for the same per-crop volatility. Critically, 50 is an upper bound on the knob's protective value: the real staple set is four (wheat, rice, maize, soy) and their failures are climatically CORRELATED, so the effective n during a breadbasket shock is closer to 2-3. Sorghum, millets, rye, cassava, sweet potato and yam have lost dietary share while soybean, sunflower and palm have gained — the direction of travel is toward higher covariance.

key_parameters.label: World synthetic nitrogen fertiliser supply
key_parameters.effect: Erisman et al.: 'Current nitrogen fertilizer use is approximately 100 Tg N per year, with 80% used for agriculture', and the Haber-Bosch process supported 48% of the global population as of 2008. First-order for a sustained cut to S Tg N/yr: fractional calorie loss is approximately 0.48 x (1 - S/100), lagged one growing season, with soil organic-N mineralisation masking roughly the first year before yields fall. This is the fastest-acting and most lethal of the four knobs because unlike a breadbasket failure it hits the ENTIRE planted area simultaneously, so no region is a supplier of last resort and grain reserves buy only the days they contain. Nitrogen supply is coupled to natural gas price rather than to any mineral reserve; phosphorus is the opposite case, a mineral chokepoint with a multi-year soil-P drawdown that acts far more slowly (see the phosphate-concentration knob of the biosphere-degradation hazard). For context on the transgression side, anthropogenic N fixation is already 190 Tg N/yr against a planetary boundary of 62 Tg N/yr — the same molecule is simultaneously a pollution boundary breach and a food-security single point of failure.

hazards.uncertainty_notes: WHERE THIS IS WEAKEST, IN ORDER. (1) The headline annual probability of 0.5%/yr is a construction, not a retrieved figure. Gaupp gives 1.1-2.0%/yr for simultaneous CLIMATE RISK across all breadbaskets in a single crop, which is a much weaker condition than a >=10% global cereal shortfall — climate risk in every region does not mean total loss in every region, and a shortfall in one crop is partly offset by others. The observational constraint runs the other way: in 65 years of FAO records there has been NO single-year global cereal production drop approaching 10%, which caps the base rate below about 1.5%/yr. I put the best estimate an order of magnitude below Gaupp's per-crop figure for that reason, and a serious critic could argue for anywhere in 0.1%-2%. (2) The accessible-stocks fraction 'a' is load-bearing and unmeasured here. The 115-day reserve figure is a world aggregate; a large share sits in national strategic reserves that do not enter trade, so an importer's effective buffer is materially smaller. I could not retrieve a figure for that share this session — it is the parameter most likely to change the tier probabilities, and it should be exposed in the simulator rather than baked in. (3) The severity tiers are author judgement calibrated on two real events with very different outcomes: 2007-08 (large price spike, no detectable global excess mortality) and historical policy famines (Bengal 1943, China 1959-61) where distribution failure rather than production failure killed tens of millions. I could not retrieve mortality estimates for either this session, so the tier death fractions are estimates, not citations. The Xia et al. nuclear-winter figures are cited only to bound the extreme tail and should not be read as this hazard's own severity. (4) The Gaupp figures come from search-surfaced abstracts; both papers are paywalled and both returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch. The two Gaupp papers are DIFFERENT studies and it is easy to blend them — the 0.3%-to-1.2% historical probabilities are from the Nature Climate Change paper, the 6%/40%/54% warming projections from the Agricultural Systems paper. Verify that attribution before compiling. (5) NO TERMINAL TIER. A food-system shock, even at the 2-billion-death scale, leaves land, seed stock, agronomic knowledge and most industrial capacity intact; recovery is bounded by herd and seed rebuilding, not by irreversibility. Ord's Table 6.1 puts existential (not catastrophic) risk from non-climate environmental damage at ~1 in 1,000 per century, and I have found no published argument for a mechanism by which agricultural failure alone ends humanity permanently. The XPT gap between catastrophe (9-20%) and extinction (1-6%) across ALL causes reinforces this: a simulator that lets this hazard terminate the run is making a claim no source in this packet supports. (6) Crop diversity is the knob I am least able to quantify: Khoury measures homogeneity of national food SUPPLIES, not the covariance of yield failures, and the step from '50 commodities supply 90% of calories' to a variance multiplier is my inference, not his finding.
cascades_into: biosphere-degradation-pollinator-and-soil-loss: emergency cropland expansion, reserve drawdown, fallow-breaking and intensified fishing during and after a shock accelerate soil, habitat and stock loss, lowering the floor for the next shock — this is the feedback loop that makes the pair worth modelling together rather than separately

conflict-and-state-fragility: food price spikes transmit to unrest and government failure in import-dependent states with a lag of months, and conflict then destroys the following season's planting, converting a one-year shock into a multi-year one

pandemic-risk: undernutrition raises infectious-disease incidence and case-fatality, so a food shock raises the death toll of a concurrent or subsequent epidemic without changing its probability of emergence

hazards.name: VEI-7 / Magnitude-7 explosive eruption (Tambora class)
hazards.one_line: An eruption of Tambora-1815 scale or larger injects tens of teragrams of sulfur into the stratosphere, cooling the planet by roughly one to two degrees for two to three years and causing simultaneous harvest failures across the mid-latitudes.
hazards.mechanism: A magnitude-7 eruption ejects on the order of 10^14 kg of magma (>=100 km3 bulk tephra) over days to weeks. Proximally, pyroclastic density currents travel 20-100+ km and would erase a city outright; ash fall collapses roofs; rain-remobilised lahars persist for a decade or more. But the global killer is the sulfur. Newhall, Self & Robock note that above roughly 5 Tg SO2 of stratospheric input, eruptions produce noticeable climate impacts; Tambora delivered ~53-60 Tg SO2 and Pinatubo's ~20 Mt SO2 alone lowered global surface temperature by 0.5 degC for two years. The sulfate aerosol veil reflects shortwave radiation, cools land faster than ocean, weakens the Asian and African monsoons and shortens growing seasons in both hemispheres simultaneously. What kills people at scale is then famine and the seizing-up of grain trade, not ash or heat: 1258 (post-Samalas) brought famine, grain-price inflation and the Spitalfields mass graves; 1816 (post-Tambora) brought the Year Without a Summer with famine across Europe, India and China. A modern repeat adds failure modes Tambora did not have: multi-week closure of global airspace, degraded GPS timing, ash-induced power-grid flashovers, and just-in-time food logistics with only months of grain in store.

annual_probability.event_definition: An eruption anywhere on Earth delivering stratospheric sulfate forcing at least as large as Tambora 1815 - equivalently VEI >= 7 / magnitude >= 7 for silicic explosive eruptions, but also reachable by high-sulfur basaltic fissure eruptions such as Laki 1783. Best estimate is the ice-core rate of forcing-events exceeding Tambora (Lin et al. 2022: 1.60 per millennium over 60-9 ka). Low bound is Rougier et al. 2018's geological M7 return period of 1200 yr; high bound is Newhall et al. 2018's incompleteness-corrected 2 per millennium.
annual_probability.trend: The eruption rate itself is flat: Lin et al. find the frequency of large eruptions across 60-9 ka is 'rather constant and comparable to that of recent times'. What rises steeply is consequence. World population was ~1 billion at Tambora and is >8 billion now; Newhall et al. record that the area around Campi Flegrei went from ~100,000 people at its last eruption to ~4.4 million, and that 20-30 million people now live within 100 km of several Indonesian and Philippine VEI-7 candidates. Supply-chain interdependence and thin grain reserves raise vulnerability further; forecasting, aid capacity and stored calories partly offset it.

severity_tiers.label: Remote vent, single eruption
severity_tiers.description: The eruption occurs at one of the many candidate volcanoes in the Kuriles, Aleutians, Kamchatka or the Andes with <1 million people inside 100 km, or is sulfur-poor. Proximal deaths in the thousands to low hundreds of thousands. Global cooling of ~0.5-1 K for 1-2 years produces one or two poor harvests; famine concentrated in import-dependent low-income countries; grain price spikes and export bans. Aviation disrupted for weeks over one or more continents.

severity_tiers.label: Tambora repeat near a population centre, or high sulfur yield
severity_tiers.description: Either the vent is one of the Indonesian, Philippine, Italian, Japanese or Central American candidates with millions inside 100 km - Newhall et al. state a VEI-7 near an urban area today could kill millions and that no evacuation of millions for months has ever been achieved - or the sulfur yield puts global land cooling near or above Tambora's -1.9 degC. Two to three consecutive globally poor harvests; multi-year famine across South Asia, the Sahel and the Horn; refugee flows needing food and shelter for months to years; sustained trade and financial disruption.

severity_tiers.label: Clustered eruptions or a hit on an already-stressed food system
severity_tiers.description: The worst realistic VEI-7 outcome: either a cluster of large sulfur-rich eruptions within years to decades (as in CE 1257, 1268, 1275, 1284, whose additive forcing Newhall et al. link to the onset of the Little Ice Age and a sustained ~0.5 K depression), or a single event landing on a food system already stressed by war, drought or export blockade. Cooling persists 5-10 years with decadal-to-centennial ocean-sea-ice feedback. Widespread famine, grain-export nationalism, state failure and resource conflict; Newhall et al. explicitly note that desperate populations now have modern weapons and that analogies have been drawn to nuclear-war scenarios.

key_parameters.label: Stratospheric SO2 injection
key_parameters.effect: Sets the global forcing. Newhall et al. give ~5 Tg SO2 as the threshold for a noticeable climate impact; Pinatubo's ~20 Mt SO2 gave -0.5 degC global mean for 2 yr; Tambora's ~53-60 Tg gave -1.9 +/- 0.2 degC over global land in 1816 (Wilson et al. 2023). The response is markedly sublinear because larger injections grow larger aerosol droplets that scatter less per unit mass and sediment faster; a defensible functional form for a simulator is dT_land ~ 1.9 K * (M / 60 Tg)^0.6, saturating above ~200 Tg.

key_parameters.label: Vent latitude
key_parameters.effect: Controls aerosol lifetime and hemispheric reach. Newhall et al.: tropical injections are carried poleward into both hemispheres by the Brewer-Dobson circulation and persist with an e-folding time scale of ~1 yr; high-latitude injections (Laki 1783, Katmai 1912) spread only to the subtropics of the same hemisphere with e-folding lifetimes of 3-5 months. Multiply integrated global forcing by roughly 1.0 for |lat| < 25 deg, ~0.3-0.5 for |lat| > 45 deg, and scale further by season for high-latitude events (little impact in autumn/winter when insolation is low).

key_parameters.label: Population within 100 km of the vent
key_parameters.effect: Sets the proximal death toll, which is roughly linear in exposed population absent successful evacuation. Newhall et al.'s Table 3 of VEI-7 candidates spans 0.0001 million (Zavaritski, Russia) to 30 million (Indonesian and Philippine candidates); the current value here is the rough median of the populated candidates. Pyroclastic flows reach 20-100 km; survival inside that radius without evacuation is near zero.

key_parameters.label: Actionable evacuation lead time
key_parameters.effect: The dominant lever on proximal mortality and the one humanity is worst at. Newhall et al. report that at Rabaul, Campi Flegrei and Pinatubo, despite prolonged early unrest, 'the final runup to eruption was just hours to days' and that Pinatubo's precursors were 'unremarkable straight through the onset of VEI 3 eruptions, until just a day before the VEI 6 climactic phase'. Historically, tens of thousands have been evacuated for months and hundreds of thousands for a few days, but never millions for months. Model proximal survival as saturating: near-zero at 0 days, ~0.5 at ~7 days, ~0.9 only beyond ~90 days, and cap achievable evacuation at ~10^6 people for multi-month durations.

key_parameters.label: Large sulfur-rich eruptions within one human lifetime
key_parameters.effect: Newhall et al.: 'When multiple large sulfur-rich eruptions occur within years or decades of each other, their influence on climate seems to be additive... Each successive eruption prolongs the volcanic cooling', and both empirical evidence and modelling suggest they can shift North Atlantic ocean circulation with effects lasting decades to centuries. Treat forcing as additive within a ~30-yr window and multiply recovery_years by roughly the count; the 13th-century cluster is the worked example, credited with initiating the Little Ice Age.

citations.claim: Definition and causes of an abrupt sunlight reduction scenario (ASRS), the framing under which a large eruption is modelled as a global food shock rather than a blast hazard.

citations.exact_figure: ASRS: "A sudden catastrophic event causes an immense amount of aerosol material of sulfates or black carbon (soot) to be projected and entrapped in the stratosphere for several years." Three causes identified: volcanic winter from a large volcanic eruption, direct impact of an exceptionally large asteroid or comet, and nuclear winter. Their modelled nuclear case uses "150 Tg of soot ... projected above the clouds" with effects lasting "several years at a minimum".

cascades_into: vei8-supereruption: drawn from the same caldera population and the same magnitude-frequency power law, so an observed excess of M7 events implies a higher M8 rate
abrupt-sunlight-reduction-famine: this is the principal non-nuclear route to a multi-year global harvest failure
